headline: Anthropic's $2T IPO debut sets a public comp for AI, then fades below $100
bottomLine: Anthropic's record $81B IPO opened up 34% then faded below $100, a live comp for Perplexity and the AI portfolio. Quartz reports Trump's accounts bought SpaceX shares near contract awards; Nvidia's board rejected Huang's return.

portfolio.title: Report says Trump's accounts bought SpaceX, Palantir shares near contract awards
portfolio.brief: Quartz reports Trump's accounts bought SpaceX and Palantir shares near federal contract awards. SpaceXSI denies liability in a UK lawmaker's Grok-images suit, and Ars reports Grok Bot ignored stop orders.
portfolio.impact: A listed holding that depends on federal awards now faces political-trading scrutiny, plus Grok legal and safety costs. Quartz is a single source, but governance headlines can move the stock fast.
portfolio.action: Confirm with fund ops today whether the first SPCX sale executed before the Nov 6 window, and decide if the Trump-accounts report changes the pace of the next tranche.

portfolio.title: Luckey urges Huang's return; Anduril adds 600-ton ship and Air Force win
portfolio.brief: Anduril co-founder Palmer Luckey said China is 'thrilled' Huang is out and wants him reinstated. Anduril and HD Hyundai launched the 600-ton ASV Alpha, and the Air Force awarded a counter-air launcher prototype.
portfolio.impact: Luckey is putting Anduril on record in the US-China chip fight, while new ship and air-defense wins widen its range beyond drones. A reported IPO within two years would reshape its next private round.
portfolio.action: Ask Anduril by Friday whether the reported IPO within two years replaces its next private round, and how it would protect contract timing if Congress caps defense spending.

thesis.title: AI froth shows, but Fed hike push and a Bitcoin death cross cut against our call
thesis.brief: The ECB flagged over $4T of Big Tech commitments, and protesters were arrested outside Nasdaq over bubble risk. CoinDesk says the Fed is pushing more rate hikes; Bitcoin entered a death cross.
thesis.impact: AI spending looks stretched, but money is tightening, not loosening. Rate hikes and a weak Bitcoin cut against our call that loose money pushes savers and sovereigns into hard assets, so that part looks early.

thesis.title: Market-structure bill hopes fade as regulators move by rule instead
thesis.brief: Ripple's Alderoty says hopes for market-structure legislation are fading. The CFTC chair outlined routes for onchain venues like Hyperliquid, and an SEC nominee wants tokenization handled by full rulemaking.
thesis.impact: The Senate passage we predicted for early 2026 hasn't happened. Clarity is arriving through slower, reversible agency rules, which delays the institutional on-ramp for tokens we expected.

thesis.title: SMR and geothermal deals advance as oil keeps flowing through Hormuz
thesis.brief: Bulgaria's NEK signed an MoU on BWRX-300 SMRs, Google signed a 50-MW geothermal deal with Quaise, and China nears a commercial SMR. Iran's ship attacks escalate even as Hormuz oil traffic surges.
thesis.impact: Firm-power deals keep coming, but oil is still moving through Hormuz, which weakens the crisis urgency behind our call. The shift now rests more on data-center power demand than on oil panic.

regulation.title: OCC issues final GENIUS Act rule; senators say state stablecoin issuers lack cover
regulation.brief: The OCC issued its final rule for payment stablecoin issuers. Senators asked Treasury for a safe harbor for state-regulated issuers; MoonPay and Dave applied for national bank charters.
regulation.impact: A federal rulebook favors nationally chartered players like Erebor over state-licensed issuers, and charter applications are already queuing up. The state safe-harbor fight decides how level the field is.
regulation.next: Treasury reply on state safe harbor pending; OCC decision on MoonPay's charter awaited
regulation.action: Ask Erebor this week whether the final OCC rule changes its charter timeline or lets it issue or hold payment stablecoins, and report back to partners.

regulation.impact: Export rules can now cut chip flows overnight, the state-action risk we flagged for AI supply chains. Chip-reliant portfolio companies carry it, and short-seller China reports add to the pressure.
regulation.next: Resumption timing not reported; watch for further US guidance

tech.title: Anthropic raises $81B in record IPO, opens up 34%, then fades below $100
tech.brief: Priced at $83 (about $1.5T fully diluted), Anthropic raised about $81B, opened at $111.50 (above $2T per Reuters) and traded near $101 by midday. Amazon and Google own nearly 30%.
tech.impact: A public AI lab at roughly $1.5T to $2T gives Perplexity and our AI portfolio a live comp. The fade below $100 and most institutional bidders getting no shares show demand outran supply, a froth signal.

tech.title: Nvidia's board rejects Huang's return, starts CEO search after earnings beat
tech.brief: Nvidia rejected Huang's offer to return, hired a search firm and kept Colette Kress as interim CEO. Its first report without him doubled quarterly revenue, and the board tightened China export oversight.
tech.impact: Demand isn't wavering, so this is leadership risk, not business risk, at the main AI-chip supplier. But Washington's China pressure now shapes Nvidia's choices, a risk for every AI company reliant on its chips.

frontier.title: SpaceX catches a Starship upper stage for the first time
frontier.brief: On Nov 14 SpaceX caught the upper stage of Starship on Flight 15, a first, per CNBC, NPR and Space. A booster malfunction stopped the planned double catch.
frontier.impact: Catching the upper stage is a step toward full reusability, which sets launch costs for the whole sector. It is one flight, not peer-reviewed science, and repeatability is unproven.
